prompt: I often change an answer at the last second. Can you tell from my history whether this is actually hurting me, and if you do not have enough data yet, how will you measure it?
actualResponse:
**No — there's no data to judge that from yet. And I want to be precise about a limitation:** your history has zero recorded attempts (all sub-tests empty), so nothing to analyse. Even once you start practising, my records show only sub-test, score and date — not per-question behaviour. So answer changes will never show up automatically; this has to be measured deliberately.

**How we'd measure it (~1 min per practice set):**
While doing a timed set, log every last-second change:
1. Question number
2. From → changed to
3. Which one was actually correct

**After 3–4 sets I'll calculate:**
- **Net effect** — changes that helped vs hurt. Clear losses = a real habit worth fixing. Break-even = it's confidence, not behaviour.
- **Timing signature** — are changes clustered in the final minutes? That separates end-of-set panic from steady second-guessing.

Point 3 is the one people skip, and it's the whole measurement — without it we only know you changed answers, not what it cost you.

Want to start the diagnostic and log changes from set one? 👉 https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/reading

prompt: My exam is tomorrow morning. What should I do tonight and tomorrow before the test? I am tempted to learn a completely new Reading strategy.
actualResponse:
**Direct answer: don't learn a new Reading strategy tonight.** That's the single worst-value move available to you. A brand-new method needs days of practice to become reliable; tonight it would only compete with the habits you already have and risk confusion tomorrow. Taper, don't learn.

**Tonight (~45 min max):**
- One short, familiar-format set (20–30 min) — from [Reading drills](https://app.oetwithdrhesham.co.uk/reading/drills) if you want, but stop at one.
- Then review your own checklist — your articles note and any error list.
- Quick format reminders you already know (not new learning): timer is always visible on screen [S3]; in Parts B & C you **cannot** highlight the answer choices [S1].
- Pack ID and confirmation, eat normally, sleep early. No marathon mocks.

**Tomorrow before the test:**
- Checklist review only — no new material, no new vocab.
- Arrive early, steady pace, trust your first answer unless you have a concrete reason to change it.
- Last-minute answer changing: tonight is not the night to overhaul it — just be aware of it.

**Skip entirely:** new strategies, new question-type techniques, full mock marathons, last-minute vocabulary lists.

You're in taper mode now — protect your energy. Good luck tomorrow. And since your exam is tomorrow, if you are ever in the exam itself, come talk to me afterwards instead — I can't help during a live sitting.

One small thing: want me to save "exam tomorrow (8 Oct)" as a note so it's on record? Say yes and I will — or skip it.
